new_mathematical_results: The literal unmodulated smooth kappa phase projects into the span of the fixed H=kappa*kappa translate family at every late aperture, including resonances. This follows from their identical real Fourier zero sets and the exact native annihilator. The original negative packet transfers to that span with the full forward approximation and energy costs retained.

The direct smooth-phase projection has explicit Fourier-tail and full normal/H1 error costs. A fixed source constant C with lambda1 sqrt(C)>1/2 makes K_C=ceil(C L^3) sufficient for any prescribed fixed negative Rayleigh margin under the existing off-line-zero hypothesis. The same-aperture first-negative cutoff is at most K_C. Margin, phase selection, and eventual aperture order remain explicit. No margin is moved to first birth.

The direct projection retains the native endpoint and pole constraints. It is not asserted to retain the original quartic packets additional exact M4=0 even or M3=M5=0 odd constraints, so no theorem needing those extra rows is invoked for the cubic witnesses.

The resulting negative Ritz direction sees a negative spectral subspace, but need not be the true ground. Its full source-zero residual, possible ground overlap, spectral gap and reciprocal/tied complements remain. At dimension1 no second-eigenvalue filter is needed; the vector is already the ground ray. In higher dimension the filter price includes1/|ground overlap| after normalization.

At the alternate cubic cutoff the existing moment-normalized inverse synthesis lower costs remain exponential. The forward projection is paid, while a stable ground reconstruction and a signed common-response bound are not supplied. This is not a new claim that actual physical errors attain a worst-case inverse bound.

The actual remaining mean response F has kernel K=phi triple derivative minus phi double derivative plus phi/4 minus Jphi/16. Its permanent old-prime plateau is -1/16. The complete local signed shell is eventually positive, but its exp(t/2) main term is exactly canceled by the retained old-prime prefix.

Actual nonnegative source-sector histories each have leading m_K exp(t/2), with m_K>=exp(-B/2)/8. Thus coefficientwise nonnegative majorants cannot provide the required smaller exponent. This does not assert that the signed F has exponent1/2 and does not exclude source-specific signed cancellation.

The complete F-Selberg relation retains all prime powers, the noncompact source-coordinate term and the delayed history. The independent classical remainder has exact lower-end correction -1/4. At a hypothetical actual right zero, the full Laurent calculation retains the same nonzero double pole of tF; its simple-pole terms cancel exactly. No exponent improvement follows from the extra half-zero alone.
